sc_statement: Account access uses device checks and second-factor prompts. Sensitive actions are logged, and balances are recorded in the ledger. Card and other regulated services are pre-launch. Independent certifications have not been completed.
sc_list_aria: Frameworks relevant to tazdan and where each one stands
sc_fw_soc2_d: Independent audit of security, availability and confidentiality controls.
sc_fw_soc2_body: tazdan has not had a SOC 2 audit and holds no SOC 2 report. If one is completed, it will be listed here.
sc_fw_pci_d: The card industry's security standard for handling card data.
sc_fw_pci_body: Card top-ups are designed to use hosted payment forms from external PCI DSS service providers. Card numbers would be entered with those providers, not stored by tazdan. tazdan does not hold a PCI DSS certification, and card top-ups are not live.
sc_fw_iso_body: tazdan is not ISO 27001 certified. If a certificate is issued, its details will be published here.
sc_fw_gdpr_d: EU privacy rules for personal data, which apply to users in the EU.
sc_fw_gdpr_body: Our Privacy Policy describes how personal data is handled. GDPR and local data protection laws may apply depending on the user and jurisdiction. You can request access, correction or deletion through support.
sc_fw_aml_d: Identity checks, sanctions screening and transaction monitoring.
sc_fw_aml_body: The app includes identity checks, screening and transaction-monitoring flows. Activation of these controls depends on the operating deployment and its provider arrangements.
sc_fw_lic_d: Authorisation to hold and move customer money.
sc_fw_lic_body: tazdan is not a licensed bank and does not yet hold a money transmission licence. Regulated services require the relevant authorisations and operating partners before launch; licence details will be published if granted.
scp_sub: How tazdan protects accounts, money and data today, and what hasn't been independently verified yet. Where something isn't done, this page says so.
scp_ops_d: The platform includes automated checks, privileged-action logs and controls for sensitive operations. Additional independent assurance is planned. The exact controls available to users depend on the operating deployment.
scp_fw_d: The frameworks that matter for a money app like tazdan, and where each one stands today.
scp_pay_d: Card top-ups are designed around hosted payment forms from external service providers. Card details would be entered there, and a deposit would be credited only after verification of the provider response. Card top-ups are not live.
scp_pay_3_d: A deposit credits only after the provider's signature checks out.
scp_acct_d: The mechanisms that protect every account. The trust page explains each one in more depth.
scp_acct_link: How your money is actually held
scp_priv_d: Our Privacy Policy describes how personal data is handled. Identity verification flows are built into the app and may rely on external providers when deployed.
scp_gap_d: A security page that lists only strengths isn't much use. This is what hasn't happened yet.
scp_gap_4: Required licences have not yet been granted.
scp_vuln_d: If you find a security issue, email security@tazdan.com with enough detail to reproduce it: the URL or endpoint, the steps, and the impact. Please report it privately and give us time to fix it before publishing.
scp_do_1: Report privately before any public disclosure
scp_do_2: Share a minimal proof of concept only
scp_do_3: Give us reasonable time to fix before publishing
scp_dont_2: Access or change other people's data or money
scp_dont_3: Use denial of service, social engineering or physical attacks
scp_cta_d: Email security@tazdan.com, or reach support through the contact page.
safety.security.hero.title: Your money, your details, *protected.*
safety.security.hero.lead: How tazdan keeps every dinar accounted for, checks risky payments before they move, and keeps your details between you and the people you choose — in plain language.
safety.security.hero.note: tazdan is pre-launch and not yet licensed. Where something isn’t done yet, this page says so.

safety.security.index.funds.title: Safety of funds
safety.security.index.funds.body: Books that must balance, and your money counted apart from ours.
safety.security.index.tx.title: Security of transactions
safety.security.index.tx.body: Only you can move your money.
safety.security.index.privacy.title: Private by design
safety.security.journey.funds.title: Every dinar, *accounted for.*
safety.security.journey.funds.body: Every movement of money is written as entries that add up to zero — and you can download a full statement of your own any time.
safety.security.journey.funds.alt: The statements screen in the tazdan app
safety.security.journey.twofa.title: A second lock, *in your pocket.*
safety.security.journey.twofa.body: Turn on an authenticator app and sensitive actions need a fresh 6-digit code from your phone. A recovery code gets you back in if you lose it.
safety.security.journey.twofa.alt: Two-factor authentication turned on in the tazdan app
safety.security.journey.devices.title: Your devices, *and only yours.*
safety.security.journey.devices.body: Every phone and computer signed in to your account is listed. Forget one, or sign out all the others in a tap — it takes effect on their very next request.
safety.security.journey.devices.alt: The trusted devices and active sessions list in the tazdan app
safety.security.journey.escrow.title: Locked in escrow *before you pay.*
safety.security.journey.escrow.body: When a trade opens, the seller’s crypto is locked in escrow. It’s released to the buyer only when the seller confirms the payment arrived. If something goes wrong, either side can open a dispute.
safety.security.journey.escrow.alt: A P2P trade held in escrow in the tazdan app
safety.security.journey.hidden.title: Balances hidden *with one tap.*
safety.security.journey.hidden.body: Privacy mode hides every balance on screen — handy in a queue or on a bus. Press and hold to peek. Market prices stay visible.
safety.security.journey.hidden.alt: Balances hidden by privacy mode in the tazdan app
safety.security.journey.handle.title: Get paid *without your bank details.*
safety.security.journey.handle.body: Share an @handle or a QR code. Nobody needs your bank account number or your phone number to pay you.
safety.security.journey.handle.alt: The receive screen with a QR code and @handle in the tazdan app
safety.security.journey.kyc.title: Verified once, *kept between us.*
safety.security.journey.kyc.body: We check your ID because the law requires it and because it keeps fraudsters out. The people you pay and trade with never see your documents.
safety.security.journey.kyc.alt: The verification level screen in the tazdan app
safety.security.pain.title: Trust is earned *in the details.*
safety.security.pain.lead: Moving money in Libya often means trusting people you can’t see — a clerk, a stranger in a cash deal, an app. This is what we changed.
safety.security.pain.1.before: A number on a screen can be changed by someone you’ll never meet.
safety.security.pain.1.after: Nobody at tazdan can edit your balance. Every change is a balanced entry, and corrections need two people.
safety.security.pain.2.before: In a cash deal, you hand over money and hope the other side delivers.
safety.security.pain.2.after: On P2P, the seller’s crypto is locked in escrow before you pay.
safety.security.pain.3.before: To get paid, you give your bank account number and phone to people you barely know.
safety.security.pain.3.after: Share an @handle or a QR code instead.
safety.security.pain.4.before: One stolen password, and the account is empty by morning.
safety.security.pain.4.after: New devices and larger payments need a fresh code — or Face ID on a phone you already trust.
safety.security.stats.1.label: How often the books are re-added in every currency
safety.security.stats.2.label: To approve a correction above the single-person limit
safety.security.stats.3.label: Checked before every withdrawal, transfer abroad and business payout
safety.security.stats.4.label: The most precise a Near me location is ever saved
safety.security.funds.title: Every dinar, *accounted for.*
safety.security.funds.lead: tazdan keeps its books the way banks and auditors do: double-entry. Money can’t appear or disappear without a matching entry somewhere else.
safety.security.funds.diagram.title: Watch a payment *being recorded.*
safety.security.funds.diagram.body: Pick a payment. Each line is an entry in tazdan’s books; together they must add up to zero, or nothing is saved.
safety.security.funds.p1.title: Checked by the database itself
safety.security.funds.p1.body: Every group of entries is added up again at the moment it’s saved. If it doesn’t balance in every currency, nothing is written.
safety.security.funds.p2.title: Nobody can type over your balance
safety.security.funds.p2.body: Your balance changes only through balanced entries. Entries can’t be edited or deleted afterwards — a mistake is fixed with a new, visible entry.
safety.security.funds.p3.title: Corrections need two people
safety.security.funds.p3.body: Adjustments above a small limit, goodwill refunds and rate overrides need a second staff member’s approval. Whoever asks can’t approve.
safety.security.funds.p4.title: Money set aside for what’s pending
safety.security.funds.p4.body: While a withdrawal, claim link, P2P trade, savings lock or business payout is pending, its money is reserved, so it can’t be spent twice.
safety.security.funds.p5.title: Each payment happens once
safety.security.funds.p5.body: A double tap, a second device or a shaky connection can’t apply the same payment twice. The repeat is refused.
safety.security.funds.p6.title: Trading stops if the books disagree
safety.security.funds.p6.body: Every five minutes, tazdan re-adds its books in every currency. If anything is off, buying, selling and converting stop automatically until a person has investigated.
safety.security.funds.p7.title: Every staff action leaves a trail
safety.security.funds.p7.body: Approvals, freezes and limit changes are logged with who did it, from where, what changed and why — in records that can’t be edited.
safety.security.partner.title: What depends on our licensed partner
safety.security.partner.body: Our books keep customer money separate from tazdan’s own. Holding that money in dedicated safeguarding bank accounts — and reconciling those accounts every day — will be arranged with the licensed banking partners we launch with. It isn’t in place yet.
safety.security.partner.body2: tazdan is not a bank. Balances are not covered by a deposit-protection or insurance scheme.
safety.ledger.label: Choose a payment to see how it’s recorded
safety.ledger.caption: Entries for this payment, in the order they’re written
safety.ledger.class.customer.title: Customer money
safety.ledger.class.customer.body: Your wallets, P2P escrow and money waiting to be sent abroad. This is money tazdan owes its customers.
safety.ledger.class.settlement.title: Money in transit
safety.ledger.class.settlement.body: Money on its way with banks, payment partners and blockchains, plus controlled corrections.
safety.ledger.class.corporate.title: tazdan’s revenue
safety.ledger.class.corporate.body: Our fees and exchange margin. For transfers abroad, they count as ours only once the money is paid out — never when you fund it.
safety.ledger.note.transfer: A payment between two tazdan users moves from one customer account to another, instantly. It never leaves customer money.
safety.ledger.note.p2p: When a trade opens, the seller’s crypto moves into escrow — still counted as customer money. It reaches the buyer only when the seller confirms the payment arrived; if the trade is cancelled, it goes back to the seller.
safety.ledger.note.remit: Money for a transfer abroad waits in its own customer account until it’s paid out. Only then does our fee count as revenue. Refunded before payout? You get everything back, fee included.
safety.ledger.note.broken: Here the entries are 10 dinars apart. The database adds up every group of entries as it’s saved and refuses any that don’t come to zero — so this one is never written.
safety.ledger.illustrative: Amounts and names are illustrative; account names are simplified.
safety.security.tx.title: Only you can *move your money.*
safety.security.tx.lead: Strong sign-in, a fresh check before risky actions and screening behind the scenes — without slowing down the payments you make every day.
safety.security.tx.sessions.title: Sign-in that watches the door
safety.security.tx.sessions.body: Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes. Sign-in tokens last 15 minutes and renew quietly; if a stolen one is ever replayed, every session is signed out at once. Signing out other devices takes effect on their next request.
safety.security.tx.stepup.title: One more check before money moves
safety.security.tx.stepup.body: Larger payments and anything from a new device ask you to confirm again — on transfers, chat payments, claim links and money sent abroad. Your limits show before you confirm, so you never wait for a code you can’t use.
safety.security.stepup.bio: Face ID on a trusted device
safety.security.tx.onchain.title: Outside wallets, added with care
safety.security.tx.onchain.body: Sending crypto out needs two-factor, a verified email and an address saved at least 24 hours earlier. If a send fails, the money comes back to your wallet.
safety.security.tx.escrow.title: Escrow on every P2P trade
safety.security.tx.escrow.body: The seller’s crypto is locked before you pay. Once you’ve marked a trade paid, it can’t simply be cancelled — a dispute goes to a person on our team.
safety.security.tx.screening.title: Screening
safety.security.tx.screening.body: Names and wallet addresses are checked against sanctions and politically exposed person watchlists before money goes to a bank, an outside wallet or another country. A possible match goes to a person — never an automatic no.
safety.security.tx.risk.title: A 17-rule risk engine
safety.security.tx.risk.body: Unusual amounts, sudden bursts, new devices and brand-new beneficiaries are weighed before every withdrawal, transfer abroad and business payout. If a rule ever fails to run, the payment waits for a person instead of going through.
safety.security.tx.limits.title: Rate limits and kill switches
safety.security.tx.limits.body: Sign-in, reset and code checks allow a handful of tries, then pause; addresses that keep failing are blocked. If something looks wrong, our team can pause one feature, currency, corridor, provider or account in seconds.
safety.security.tx.custody.title: Encrypted custody
safety.security.tx.custody.body: The master key behind tazdan’s crypto wallets is encrypted with AES-256-GCM. In production it is designed to be sealed by a cloud key-management service, so access to the database alone can’t unlock it.
safety.security.tx.webhooks.title: Signed webhooks and hashed keys for businesses
safety.security.tx.webhooks.body: Business notifications carry an HMAC-SHA256 signature with a timestamp, go only to HTTPS addresses and never to private networks. API keys are 192-bit random, stored only as hashes and shown once.
safety.security.privacy.title: Your details *stay yours.*
safety.security.privacy.lead: Getting paid shouldn’t mean handing a stranger your bank account number, your phone number or your address. tazdan shows the people you deal with only what they need.
safety.security.privacy.alt: Turning on privacy mode in the tazdan app
safety.security.privacy.handle.title: Pay by @handle
safety.security.privacy.handle.body: Pay and get paid with an @handle or a QR code. No bank account number or phone number to give out.
safety.security.privacy.claim.title: Claim links
safety.security.privacy.claim.body: Send money by link to someone who isn’t on tazdan yet. Add a PIN, cancel any time before it’s claimed, and unclaimed money comes back to you when the link expires. The link itself carries no personal details.
safety.security.privacy.p2p.title: First name, last initial
safety.security.privacy.p2p.body: In the P2P marketplace, other people see your first name and last initial with your real trade record — not your full name.
safety.security.privacy.mode.title: Privacy mode
safety.security.privacy.mode.body: Hide every balance on screen with one tap; press and hold to peek. Your public profile stays off unless you switch it on.
safety.security.privacy.staff.title: Need-to-know inside tazdan
safety.security.privacy.staff.body: Contact details are masked for staff whose role doesn’t need them. Where AI helps our team, emails, phone numbers and account numbers are masked first — and AI is off in production by default.
safety.security.privacy.less.title: We keep less
safety.security.privacy.less.body: Exact locations, passwords, payment confirmation codes, session tokens and API keys are never stored as they are — only rounded or hashed versions.
safety.security.seen.title: What other people see
safety.security.seen.body: Only what they need to pay you or trade with you.
safety.security.seen.1: Your @handle and name, when you pay or chat
safety.security.seen.2: First name and last initial, in the P2P marketplace
safety.security.seen.3: Your completed trades and completion rate
safety.security.seen.4: A rough distance — only if you turned on Near me
safety.security.never.title: What they never see
safety.security.never.body: However you pay, these stay with you.
safety.security.privacy.sharing: We share personal data only as our Privacy Policy describes — for example with regulators when the law requires it, and with the verification and payment partners that process your transactions.
safety.near.title: Near me, *without your address.*
safety.near.body: Find P2P sellers close by without anyone learning where you are.
safety.near.s1.title: You choose to share
safety.near.s1.body: Near me is off until you turn it on — for a listing, or for a single search. The app never asks for your location in the background.
safety.near.s2.title: Rounded before it’s saved
safety.near.s2.body: A listing keeps only a point rounded to about a kilometre. Your exact spot is never stored.
safety.near.s3.title: Only a rough distance is shown
safety.near.s3.body: Other people see a distance like “1 km” or “15 km” — never a pin, a map or coordinates.
safety.security.kyc.line: We verify who you are once, so nobody else needs to know.
safety.security.kyc.title: Private, *not anonymous.*
safety.security.kyc.body: tazdan verifies every customer and screens payments, as the law requires — that’s what keeps stolen identities and fraud out. What we promise is that your details aren’t handed to the people you pay, the strangers you trade with, or staff without a reason to look.

safety.security.notyet.pentest.title: External penetration test
safety.security.notyet.pentest.body: Scoped, not yet carried out. We’ll publish a summary when it’s done.
safety.security.notyet.audits.title: Independent security audits
safety.security.notyet.audits.body: Formal third-party audits of our security controls are planned alongside licensing. Reports will be listed in the trust centre as they’re completed.
safety.security.notyet.safeguarding.body: Customer money is separated in our books today. Dedicated safeguarding bank accounts and their daily reconciliation depend on the licensed banking partner.
safety.security.notyet.kms.title: Cloud key management for custody
safety.security.notyet.kms.body: The master key is encrypted today; sealing it with a cloud key-management service is a launch requirement.
safety.security.notyet.licence.title: Licensing
safety.security.notyet.licence.body: Engaging with the Central Bank of Libya on licensing. tazdan is not licensed yet.

safety.security.faq.title: Security, *answered.*
safety.security.faq.1.q: Can someone at tazdan change my balance?
safety.security.faq.1.a: No. Balances change only through balanced entries, and entries can’t be edited afterwards. If a correction is ever needed, it’s a new entry — and above a small limit it needs a second staff member’s approval.
safety.security.faq.2.q: Is my money protected like a bank deposit?
safety.security.faq.2.a: No. tazdan isn’t a bank and balances aren’t covered by a deposit-protection scheme. Customer money is kept separate from tazdan’s in our books; dedicated safeguarding accounts will be set up with the licensed banking partners we launch with.
safety.security.faq.3.q: What if I lose my phone?
safety.security.faq.3.a: Sign in on another device and remove the lost phone from your trusted devices, or sign out every other device at once. If you use two-factor authentication, your recovery code gets you back in.
safety.security.faq.4.q: If tazdan verifies my ID, who else can see my details?
safety.security.faq.4.a: Not the people you pay or trade with: they see your @handle and name, or just your first name and last initial on P2P. Inside tazdan, contact details are masked for staff who don’t need them. We share data with others only as our Privacy Policy describes.
safety.security.faq.5.q: Will someone I trade with on P2P know where I live?
safety.security.faq.5.a: No. Near me is opt-in, your location is rounded to about a kilometre before it’s saved, and other people only ever see a rough distance.
safety.security.faq.6.q: Why was I asked for a code when I’m already signed in?
safety.security.faq.6.a: Larger payments and actions from a new device ask you to confirm again. It takes a few seconds and means a stolen session alone can’t move your money.

safety.trust.disclosures.title: Important *to know.*
safety.trust.disclosure.1: Crypto assets are volatile. The value of what you hold can fall sharply, even to zero. Never put in more than you can afford to lose.
safety.trust.disclosure.2: tazdan is not a bank. Balances held on the platform are not protected by a government deposit-insurance scheme.
safety.trust.disclosure.3: Nothing on this site or in the app is financial advice. Past prices say nothing about future ones.
safety.trust.disclosure.4: P2P trades are between users. tazdan provides escrow and dispute handling but is not a party to the trade.
safety.trust.disclosure.5: Services may be restricted in some countries. It’s your responsibility to follow the laws where you live.
safety.trust.disclosure.6: Cards are not available. A future card would be issued by a regulated issuing partner under its own terms.
safety.trust.disclosure.7: tazdan may freeze or close accounts that break our terms, our anti-money-laundering rules or the law.
safety.trust.cta.title: Questions? *Ask us directly.*
safety.trust.cta.lead: We’d rather answer than have you guess. Or join the waitlist and be among the first in.
safety.compliance.hero.title: Keeping crime out, *so honest money moves.*
safety.compliance.hero.lead: Verifying customers, screening payments and keeping records are how a money app earns the right to exist. Here is how tazdan does it — and what it means for you.
safety.compliance.hero.note: These are controls built into tazdan’s software. They aren’t legal advice, don’t describe a licensed activity and don’t imply any regulatory approval.
safety.compliance.honest.title: What it means *for you.*
safety.compliance.honest.lead: Most of this runs quietly in the background. When it does touch you, this is why.
safety.compliance.honest.1.after: The law requires it — and it keeps stolen identities and mule accounts away from the people you pay.
safety.compliance.honest.2.after: Checks run automatically before money leaves. A payment waits only when something about it is unusual.
safety.compliance.honest.3.before: “What if they ask where my money came from?”
safety.compliance.honest.3.after: For larger transfers abroad we may ask — a payslip, bank statement or business papers, for example. Answering quickly is the fastest way through.
safety.compliance.honest.4.before: “What happens to my money while they look?”
safety.compliance.honest.4.after: It stays reserved, not lost. A transfer abroad refunded before payout comes back in full, fee included.
safety.compliance.kyc.title: Verification, *one level at a time.*
safety.compliance.kyc.lead: Each level unlocks higher limits. The app shows your live limits and what the next level unlocks.
safety.compliance.kyc.alt: The verification screen with levels and live limits in the tazdan app
safety.compliance.kyc.l0.title: Not verified
safety.compliance.kyc.l0.body: Explore the app and send small amounts. Withdrawals stay locked until you verify.
safety.compliance.kyc.l1.title: Level 1 · Identity
safety.compliance.kyc.l1.body: An ID document and a selfie holding it.
safety.compliance.kyc.l2.title: Level 2 · Address
safety.compliance.kyc.l2.body: Proof of address — a utility bill or bank statement from the last three months.
safety.compliance.kyc.l3.title: Level 3 · Source of funds
safety.compliance.kyc.l3.body: A payslip, bank statement or business papers. The highest limits.
safety.compliance.kyc.limits.title: Limits you see before you confirm
safety.compliance.kyc.limits.body: Per-payment, daily and monthly limits are shown before you confirm, with the date they reset — daily at midnight and monthly on the 1st, Tripoli time.
safety.compliance.kyc.review.title: Reviewed by a person
safety.compliance.kyc.review.body: Documents are reviewed by our verification team and every decision is recorded. Applying for a higher level never lowers the one you have.
safety.compliance.kyc.kyb.title: Businesses verify too
safety.compliance.kyc.kyb.body: Business accounts go through KYB. Payouts stay off until compliance approves, and the owner is told the outcome.
safety.compliance.screen.title: Checked against the lists *that matter.*
safety.compliance.screen.lead: Before money leaves tazdan, the people and wallets involved are checked against sanctions and politically exposed person watchlists.
safety.compliance.screen.who.title: Who is checked
safety.compliance.screen.who.body: You, when you send money abroad or withdraw; beneficiaries when they’re added and again over time; businesses and the people they pay; and crypto destination addresses.
safety.compliance.screen.how.title: How matching works
safety.compliance.screen.how.body: Names are compared after removing accents, honorifics and Arabic spelling variants, checked against aliases, and weighed with date of birth and country. Wallet addresses must match exactly.
safety.compliance.screen.person.title: A person decides
safety.compliance.screen.person.body: A possible match is reviewed by our compliance team. Similar-looking names never trigger an automatic rejection.
safety.compliance.screen.geo.title: Restricted countries
safety.compliance.screen.geo.body: Transfers abroad and business payouts involving restricted jurisdictions are refused.
safety.compliance.screen.lists.title: Lists with a source
safety.compliance.screen.lists.body: Official lists — such as the UN, US, EU and UK sanctions lists — are loaded by our compliance team, with the source and date of each import kept.
safety.compliance.monitor.title: Seventeen rules, *before money moves.*
safety.compliance.monitor.lead: A risk engine checks every withdrawal, transfer abroad and business payout in real time — before it runs, not after.
safety.compliance.monitor.rules.title: What the rules look for
safety.compliance.monitor.rules.body: Seventeen rules in four groups. We don’t publish thresholds — that would only help the people they’re meant to stop. Rule changes are versioned and logged with a reason.
safety.compliance.rules.geo.title: Geography
safety.compliance.rules.sanctions.title: Sanctions
safety.compliance.rules.sanctions.body: A possible watchlist match, or no list coverage for a check.
safety.compliance.rules.aml.title: Money-laundering patterns
safety.compliance.rules.aml.body: Large amounts, sudden bursts, amounts split to stay under limits, money cycled straight back out, missing source of funds, and a combined risk score.
safety.compliance.rules.fraud.title: Fraud patterns
safety.compliance.rules.fraud.body: Brand-new beneficiaries and accounts, one payout account shared by many senders, new or shared devices, and recent password or two-factor changes.
safety.compliance.outcome.title: What can *happen next.*
safety.compliance.outcome.lead: Every decision is stored with the rules it triggered and a plain-language explanation for our team.
safety.compliance.outcome.approve.title: Approve
safety.compliance.outcome.approve.body: Nothing unusual — the payment goes ahead.
safety.compliance.outcome.challenge.body: A step-up check, for example a larger payment from a new device.
safety.compliance.outcome.review.title: Hold for review
safety.compliance.outcome.review.body: The money stays reserved while a person looks, or we ask you for more information.
safety.compliance.outcome.refuse.title: Refuse
safety.compliance.outcome.refuse.body: The payment doesn’t go ahead and a case is opened. If a rule ever fails to run, the payment is held for a person — it’s never waved through.
safety.compliance.cases.title: Every flag reaches *a person.*
safety.compliance.cases.lead: A held payment opens a case. Nobody’s account is decided by a rule alone.
safety.compliance.cases.sla.title: An owner and a deadline
safety.compliance.cases.sla.body: Each case has a priority and a deadline — from 4 hours for the most urgent to 7 days for routine ones.
safety.compliance.cases.file.title: A case file that can’t be rewritten
safety.compliance.cases.file.body: Notes and decisions are append-only, and a case can’t be closed without a written resolution.
safety.compliance.cases.roles.title: The right people, and only them
safety.compliance.cases.roles.body: Compliance and AML-analyst roles handle cases; a read-only auditor role can review everything without changing anything.
safety.compliance.records.title: Records that *can’t be rewritten.*
safety.compliance.records.lead: The evidence an auditor or regulator needs is kept from the first day — and you can download your own statements any time.
safety.compliance.records.alt: The statements screen in the tazdan app
safety.compliance.records.kept.title: Append-only by design
safety.compliance.records.kept.body: Ledger entries, status changes, staff actions, risk decisions, case notes and security events are protected by the database against edits and deletion.
safety.compliance.records.quotes.title: The price you saw, kept as shown
safety.compliance.records.quotes.body: A quote for a transfer abroad can’t be changed after it’s issued.
safety.compliance.records.retention.body: Financial-crime rules require some records to be kept even after an account closes. Our Privacy Policy and account deletion page explain what we keep and for how long.
safety.compliance.abroad.title: Who sends, who receives, *and why.*
safety.compliance.abroad.lead: Every transfer abroad carries the information a payout partner and a regulator expect to see.
safety.compliance.abroad.sender.title: A verified sender
safety.compliance.abroad.sender.body: Sent from a verified tazdan account, within that account’s limits, after a step-up check where needed.
safety.compliance.abroad.beneficiary.bod: Bank details are validated (IBANs by checksum) and the beneficiary is screened when added.
safety.compliance.abroad.purpose.title: A purpose, and source of funds when needed
safety.compliance.abroad.purpose.body: Each transfer records its purpose; above a corridor’s threshold, we ask where the money came from.
safety.compliance.abroad.quote.title: A locked, recorded price
safety.compliance.abroad.quote.body: The quote you accept is kept unchanged with the transfer, alongside every status change.
safety.compliance.abroad.note: Send abroad is a pilot on sandbox rails: no real money leaves tazdan until a licensed payout partner is live for each corridor.
safety.compliance.later.title: Not built *yet.*
safety.compliance.later.lead: Some parts of a full compliance programme come with the licensed operating company. This is where they stand.
safety.compliance.later.reporting.title: Regulatory reporting
safety.compliance.later.reporting.body: Filing suspicious-activity reports with the relevant financial intelligence unit will be set up with the licensed entity. The evidence is already kept in cases and logs.
safety.compliance.later.travel.title: Travel-rule messaging
safety.compliance.later.travel.body: Exchanging sender and beneficiary details directly with partner institutions isn’t built yet.
safety.compliance.later.reverify.title: Periodic re-verification
safety.compliance.later.reverify.body: Scheduled re-checks of customers and tracking of document expiry are planned.
safety.compliance.later.programme.title: Written AML programme and compliance officer
safety.compliance.later.programme.body: A programme is drafted; its adoption and the appointment of a money-laundering reporting officer come with the licensed entity.
safety.compliance.later.licence.title: Licensing
safety.compliance.later.licence.body: Engaging with the Central Bank of Libya on licensing. tazdan is not licensed yet.
safety.compliance.concern.title: Report a concern
safety.compliance.concern.body: If you’re worried about fraud, financial crime or a compliance issue involving tazdan or another user, contact us. Reports are handled confidentially.
safety.compliance.faq.title: Compliance, *answered.*
safety.compliance.faq.1.q: Why does tazdan need my ID if I’m only sending small amounts?
safety.compliance.faq.1.a: You can explore the app and send small amounts before you verify. Withdrawals and higher limits need verification, because the law requires it and because it keeps fraud out.
safety.compliance.faq.2.a: tazdan’s verification team — and, where one is used, our identity-verification provider, as the Privacy Policy describes. The people you pay or trade with never see them.
safety.compliance.faq.3.a: Now and then a payment needs a second look by a person. Your money stays reserved while that happens. We can’t always share the reason for a decision — that’s a legal rule, not a judgement about you.
safety.compliance.faq.4.a: Not yet. We’re engaging with the Central Bank of Libya on licensing, and we’ll publish licence details only once they’re granted.
safety.compliance.disclaimer: Technical description of controls implemented in software. It is not legal advice, does not describe a licensed activity and implies no regulatory approval.
safety.compliance.cta.title: Honest money, *moving freely.*
